evidence: AI-cluster bandwidth, reliability and power demands are driving rapid adoption of high-speed copper and optical interconnects; Q1 revenue grew 114.7% YoY.
counter_evidence: Connectivity architectures can shift rapidly toward optical/NPO/CPO alternatives and large customers can change vendors at design cycles.

evidence: AEC volume accounted for over 90% of the YoY revenue increase and management disclosed hyperscaler ramps; ZeroFlap products target link-flap reliability and power/performance constraints.
counter_evidence: Public evidence does not quantify customer-level TCO savings or contract economics across the customer base.
missing_data: Independent customer ROI and renewal/repurchase economics.

evidence: Credo's proprietary SerDes/DSP portfolio spans AEC, retimers, optics and chiplets, while hyperscaler design wins can create qualification and reliability switching costs.
Oracle-related ZeroFlap development and standards participation support ecosystem relevance.
counter_evidence: Revenue remains concentrated and design wins are not permanent; optical transitions and competing silicon vendors could narrow the moat.
missing_data: Long-run design-win retention and share data by hyperscaler/platform.

evidence: The fabless model has low physical capex and GAAP operating margin reached 25.2% while revenue more than doubled.
counter_evidence: Q1 OCF-capex-SBC was approximately negative $5M and working-capital outflow was $151.3M, so reported earnings have not yet translated cleanly into per-share owner cash.
A clean incremental ROIC cohort is unavailable because R&D, SBC and acquisition economics are intermixed.
missing_data: Normalized multi-quarter owner cash per share and post-acquisition return on invested capital.

evidence: Management has expanded the product portfolio aggressively and maintained substantial liquidity after acquisition activity.
counter_evidence: DustPhotonics consideration was about $1.251B with roughly $896M goodwill, making integration and return-on-acquisition execution material.
Q1 SBC was about 18.4% of revenue, a meaningful shareholder cost.
missing_data: DustPhotonics revenue, margin and cash return contribution by period.

evidence: Cash plus short-term investments were approximately $764M and working capital about $1.3B; the core business is profitable.
counter_evidence: The $735.6M acquisition cash outflow materially reduced liquidity and purchase commitments remain meaningful.

evidence: At $160.31, unchanged Base value is about $158.20, materially closer to fair value than the prior $170.57 reference.
Reverse expectations require about 18.2% annual growth for years 2-10 under a 22%-24% owner-cash margin path and 22x terminal multiple.

reverse_expectations.growth_basis: Year-1 revenue anchor fixed; uniform growth years 2-10 (milestone paths retain fixed capital costs).
reverse_expectations.warning: Conditional on Base margins, capital claims and terminal assumptions; not an observable unique market forecast.

red_team.independence: Same analyst/model; adversarial self-review, not independent committee review.

attacks.attack: AEC demand is a temporary hyperscaler build spike.
attacks.response: Possible; multi-quarter hyperscaler diversification and Q2/Q3 growth durability are required.

attacks.attack: Optics/CPO adoption erodes copper AEC economics faster than Credo can transition.
attacks.response: Portfolio expansion into optics mitigates but does not eliminate this risk.

attacks.attack: Customer concentration makes current revenue quality fragile.
DustPhotonics was overpaid and goodwill will be impaired.
attacks.response: Large goodwill makes this a real capital-allocation risk; post-acquisition cash returns must be tracked.

attacks.attack: SBC makes GAAP earnings overstate shareholder economics.
attacks.response: Owner-cash diagnostics subtract SBC; dilution remains under investigation.

attacks.attack: Working-capital build signals channel stuffing or weak collections.
attacks.response: No such conclusion is established, but AR/inventory conversion must normalize.

attacks.attack: Gross margin will compress as AEC mix scales.
attacks.response: Q1 gross margin already declined; model uses owner cash margins well below non-GAAP margin.

attacks.attack: Large hyperscalers can dual-source and pressure price.
attacks.response: Qualification/reliability helps but customer bargaining power remains high.

attacks.attack: Base terminal multiple 22x is too generous for a cyclical semiconductor supplier.
attacks.response: This is a valid sensitivity; current price lacks a wide margin of safety even under the Base multiple.

attacks.attack: Current triple-digit growth causes investors to extrapolate an unsustainable curve.
attacks.response: Reverse expectations are lower than current growth, but maintaining 18%+ for nine years still requires durable structural leadership.

completion_gate.scope: Research composition and audit lineage complete; unresolved facts and veto investigations are NOT marked resolved.

notes: SEC filing and SEC-hosted earnings exhibit dominate financial evidence.
Market price is secondary reference only.

falsifiers: A major hyperscaler design loss plus two or more quarters of weakening AEC/optical growth and per-share owner cash would invalidate the widening-moat thesis.
increase_evidence: Top-customer concentration falls while aggregate growth remains strong.
OCF-capex-SBC turns sustainably positive and grows faster than diluted shares for at least two reporting periods.
DustPhotonics produces measurable revenue/cash returns without further large capital calls.
Price offers a material discount to conservative Base value rather than merely matching Base.
sell_evidence: Major hyperscaler design loss, sustained gross-margin erosion, or evidence that optical architecture shifts bypass Credo.
Persistent SBC/net dilution without commensurate per-share owner-cash growth.
DustPhotonics integration destroys capital or requires repeated external financing.
